description:
FILED s471a (Opus, 2026-09-06), by a #1271 probe.  PRE-EXISTING.

    my $fh; open($fh, "<", "/nonexistent");   # fails
    my $r = close($fh);

    perl 5.40.3 : $r is "" -- DEFINED and false
    PCL         : $r is undef

Same family as #403 (a filetest's FALSE is a DEFINED "" when the stat
succeeded) and #416 (s/// no-match returns "" not 0): PCL conflates perl's
false-but-defined with undef, so `defined(close $fh)` takes the wrong branch
while `if (close $fh)` is right.

Every other closed-handle answer already MATCHES perl (measured s471a,
scratch/s471a/p1271): `fileno` undef, `<$fh>` undef, `print {$fh}` undef,
`eof` 1, `binmode` undef.  This is the only one left, which is why it is worth
one line rather than a campaign.

Look at p-close's "no stream" arm in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp.  Probe the OTHER
close failures before changing it -- `close` on an already-closed handle and on
a handle whose child exited non-zero are perl's other two false answers and
they may not agree with each other.

=== DONE (s473f) ===
FIXED.  Five failing shapes probed 5.40.3 and all five answer a DEFINED "":
a handle whose open failed, one already closed, a bareword never opened, a
bareword whose open failed, a bareword already closed.  A fork-pipe whose child
exited non-zero is the sixth.  +p-close-false+ is the one constant.

`closedir` IS NOT THE SAME FACT -- probed: its failure answer is UNDEF -- which
is why the two have separate answers and not a shared one.  The
dirhandle-path entry is already the openness marker, so a second closedir sees
no entry and answers undef the way perl does with no new state.

$! is part of it: a close or closedir with NO OPEN HANDLE sets EBADF (9); one
that failed for another reason leaves $! alone (perl reads errno 0 after a
non-zero pipe child -- probed, so no blanket EBADF).

Guard Pl/t/handle-place-01.t rows 30-46.  Commit 5a952fce.
subject: close() on a NEVER-OPENED handle returns undef where perl returns a DEFINED empty string (the #403/#416 family)
